_comment: Validation target for the February 2022 Starlink loss. All values from Baruah et al. (2024) unless noted. This file is the answer key: the simulator is graded against it. Do not modify values to make the model agree.

event.name: Starlink Group 4-7 loss
event.source: Baruah et al. 2024, Space Weather 22, e2023SW003716

orbit._note: Real insertion was elliptical with ~210 km perigee. The circular assumption is a documented model limitation (PHYSICS.md section 10.1).

satellite_as_modelled_by_paper._comment: These are the paper's own modelling choices. Use these EXACTLY for validation. They are not necessarily the best physical values.
satellite_as_modelled_by_paper._cd_warning: The paper uses Cd = 1.0, stated explicitly as a simplification for comparative analysis. Running validation at 2.2 roughly doubles drag and the model reenters far too early. Validate at 1.0.
satellite_as_modelled_by_paper._ram_area_note: The paper describes these as the expected range from assumed 'open book' and 'shark fin' configurations. Treat as bounding cases, not as two discrete attitudes.
satellite_as_modelled_by_paper._thrust_note: Zero. The paper models drag alone. SpaceX commanded the fleet into a low-drag survival attitude with orbit-raising suspended.
satellite_as_modelled_by_paper._model_note: This project uses NRLMSIS 2.1 via pymsis. Exact agreement is not expected. Report the discrepancy; do not tune to hide it.

validation_targets._comment: Reproduce these. Record whatever you get, including failures.

cases.description: Reaches unrecoverable altitude by the reference time
Decays only ~7 km by the reference time

validation_targets.acceptance: Agreement within roughly 20% on decay timing is a good result and should be reported as such. A documented discrepancy with a hypothesis about its cause is stronger than a suspicious exact match.

space_weather_context._significance: The paper's central finding: space weather alone did not cause the loss. It combined with low-altitude insertion and a low ballistic coefficient. Do not present this as 'a storm killed them'.
space_weather_context._swarm_note: Swarm C is at ~434 km. Storm density enhancement is weaker at 210 km. Do not apply these percentages at insertion altitude.

corroborating_sources._comment: Other published analyses of the same event. Useful for the writeup; counts vary slightly between studies.

kataoka_2022.citation: Kataoka et al. 2022, J. Space Weather Space Clim. 12, 41

zhang_2022.citation: Zhang et al. 2022, Space Weather 20, e2022SW003168

guarnieri_2023.note: NORAD tracking analysis; suggests possible immediate loss of 32

corroborating_sources._discrepancy_note: Published loss counts range from 32 to 40. Use 38 as the primary figure and mention the spread in the writeup. This variation is itself worth noting.
